audit.whatIsWrong: Teemo's Q is called "Blinding Shot" in spikes[0], wants.you[0] and whys[1]. The ability is Blinding Dart.
audit.why: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json lists slot Q names as ["Blinding Dart"]. "Blinding Shot" is not a League ability.

audit.whatIsWrong: Quinn's ultimate is called "Tag Team" in mid, wants.foe[2] and whys[4].
audit.why: champ-data/_kits/quinn.json lists slot R as "Behind Enemy Lines" (its finisher is Skystrike). Tag Team was the pre-2015 name and no longer exists.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four separate places say Vault knocks Teemo up or knocks him back (spikes[3], wants.foe[0], early, late).
audit.why: Riot's own text for Vault: Quinn dashes TO the enemy, deals damage, slows the target, then leaps off and lands near her maximum attack range away. The displacement is on Quinn, not on Teemo. The kit's derived flags for Vault are dash + slow only — no knockup, no hardCC.
audit.corrected: Vault damages, slows and briefly interrupts you; Quinn is the one who ends up repositioned, landing at her attack range away from you.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry never says that Vault is a targeted dash, and 'early' tells the player to sidestep it with Move Quick.
audit.why: Vault is a unit-targeted dash (range 675). Once cast it cannot be dodged by movement — Move Quick only helps you stay outside 675 before she casts.
audit.corrected: Move Quick keeps you out of Vault's 675 range; it does not dodge a Vault that is already cast.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] says Quinn's first item "lets her proc Harrier through your Blind".
audit.why: Harrier is a bonus-damage basic attack. Blind makes basic attacks miss, so a blinded Quinn cannot cash a Harrier mark at all — no item changes that. Blinding Dart is 7s at every rank, which is the reason this matchup is playable.
audit.corrected: A blinded Quinn cannot cash her Harrier mark at all; the item race is about whether her burst outpaces your poison, not about beating the blind.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flags zero cooldown-sequencing cues. The entry repeatedly says "track Vault" but never gives a number.
audit.why: Vault is 12/11/10/9/8s; Blinding Dart is a flat 7s at every rank. Teemo's blind is therefore always up more often than Quinn's escape, and that gap (5s at rank 1, 1s at rank 5) is the whole matchup.
audit.corrected: Trade in the window after Vault: 12s at rank 1, and your Q is back in 7 regardless of rank.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere explains what Quinn's Q actually does to Teemo. The full layer even calls the lane a "Blind war".
audit.why: Blinding Assault marks the target and hinders its vision — it is a nearsight, not a blind. Your autos and your Toxic Shot poison keep landing through it at full damage; you simply cannot see far. Playing it as though your autos are disabled gives away free trades.
audit.corrected: Blinding Assault shrinks your vision, it does not stop your attacks — keep auto-poking through it.

audit.whatIsWrong: tldr and dosFull[1] both instruct the player to build MR against Quinn.
audit.why: Quinn is an AD marksman/assassin: Harrier's bonus damage and Vault are physical, and her whole pattern is basic attacks. Magic resist does nothing here; armour and attack-speed-slow boots are the answer.

audit.whatIsWrong: full.phases[0].why says "AA-poke + E poison wins almost every melee level 1" — Quinn is not melee.
audit.why: Quinn is a ranged marksman. The level-1 argument that actually applies is that Toxic Shot stacks on every auto while she has no ability yet to answer it.
audit.corrected: Ranged mirror at 1 — Toxic Shot stacks on every auto and she has nothing yet to stop it.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid says your Q is "fully ranked" at levels 4-5.
audit.why: Rank 5 on any ability needs level 9. More usefully, Blinding Dart's cooldown is flat 7s at every rank, so ranking it up changes damage and blind duration, never its availability.
audit.corrected: Blinding Dart is 7 seconds at every rank — it is up for every trade from level 1 onward.

edits.before: Blinding Shot shuts off Quinn's Harrier-proc autos entirely — she cannot trade back through your Q, and your poison stacks accumulate while she walks away.
edits.after: Blinding Dart shuts off Quinn's Harrier-proc autos entirely — she cannot cash a Harrier mark while blind, and your poison keeps ticking as she walks away.

edits.before: Quinn's passive Harrier procs turn her into a high-mobility burst threat — she can kite your mushrooms, gap-close with Vault to knock you up, and out-damage you in extended skirmishes.
edits.after: Quinn's passive Harrier procs turn her into a high-mobility burst threat — she can kite your mushrooms, Vault in for the slow and leap back out to attack range, and out-damage you in long skirmishes.

edits.before: Land Blinding Shot before Quinn can activate a Harrier proc — her bonus physical damage on marked targets is her entire trade pattern
edits.after: Land Blinding Dart before Quinn can cash a Harrier mark — a blinded basic attack misses, so the bonus physical damage simply never happens

edits.before: Use Vault to knock you back, interrupt your auto-poison loop, and reset the trade on her terms
edits.after: Use Vault to slow you and interrupt the poison loop, then land at her attack range with the trade reset

edits.before: Roam with Tag Team to snowball other lanes the moment you shove in and recall, flipping the map before your split-push matters
edits.after: Roam with Behind Enemy Lines the moment you shove in and recall, flipping the map before your split-push ever starts to matter

edits.before: Both of you are ranged, but your Level 1 is stronger than hers — your E poison stacks on every auto and she has no way to stop it before Quinn hits 2 and gets Vault. Poke freely with autos plus the poison trail, but never commit your Blinding Shot preemptively; hold it so that the moment she marks you with a Harrier proc and moves to cash it, you Q her and erase the bonus damage entirely. She trades best when she lands Vault first to knock you back, then follows up on the proc — so watch her body language and use Move Quick the instant you see the Vault animation, because sidestepping it denies her the entire trade sequence.
edits.after: Both of you are ranged, but your Level 1 is stronger than hers — your E poison stacks on every auto and she has no way to stop it before Quinn hits 2 and gets Vault. Poke freely with autos plus the poison trail, but never commit your Blinding Dart preemptively; hold it so that the moment she marks you with a Harrier proc and moves to cash it, you Q her and erase the bonus damage entirely. Vault is a targeted dash, so once it is cast no amount of movement dodges it — the answer is range, not reflexes. Use Move Quick to sit outside its 675 units while it is up, and step in to trade only in the 12 seconds after she spends it at rank 1.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your cleanest control window: Q is fully ranked, mushrooms can sit in every brush she might duck into, and every time she uses Vault offensively she loses her only escape from your pattern. Force her to choose between using Vault to poke-trade or saving it to disengage — she cannot do both. At 6 Tag Team gives her global roam pressure, so the moment she shoves and backs, ping your jungler and track the minimap; a Quinn that gets a free roam kill is more dangerous than one who outplayed you in lane.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your cleanest control window: Blinding Dart is a flat 7 seconds at every rank while Vault is still 11, so you get a free blind in every wave, and each Vault she spends on offence is one she does not have to escape. Force her to choose between Vault to poke-trade or Vault to disengage — she cannot do both. At 6 Behind Enemy Lines gives her global roam pressure, so the moment she shoves and backs, ping your jungler and watch the minimap; a Quinn who gets a free roam kill is more dangerous than one who outplayed you in lane.

edits.before: Quinn's 2+ items outpace yours in a direct skirmish — her Harrier burst and mobile kite mean she no longer has to commit Vault just to trade, she can proc and disengage freely. Shift into a vision-and-split role: shroom every side-lane bush and jungle entrance, deny her safe roaming corridors, and force her to answer your split-push rather than grouping for free picks. In teamfights, peel away from her line of sight; if she Vaults you in a 5v5 you are knocked up and dead before mushrooms matter.
edits.after: Quinn's 2+ items outpace yours in a direct skirmish — her Harrier burst and mobile kite mean she no longer has to commit Vault just to trade, she can proc and disengage freely. Shift into a vision-and-split role: shroom every side-lane bush and jungle entrance, deny her safe roaming corridors, and force her to answer your split-push rather than grouping for free picks. In teamfights hold Blinding Dart for the Vault: she lands at attack range and every follow-up auto misses for the duration.

edits.after: Your E poison and auto poke hit harder than her unprocced autos at Level 1 — you set the damage tone before Vault ever comes online.

edits.after: Blinding Dart cancels her Harrier-proc follow-up completely; she traded her Level 2 spike to get Vault, but Q just erases the bonus hit she was banking on.

edits.after: Behind Enemy Lines gives her global roam and Vault is down to 10s; she can leave lane freely, so every push you make may just feed her a kill elsewhere.

edits.after: Blind her autos, build armor, out-poke her. Teemo owns the 12s window after her Vault.

notes:
DERIVED-FLAG FALSE POSITIVE affecting this champion globally: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json flags Noxious Trap (R) with "knockup". Mushrooms slow and damage over time; they do not displace. The flag was almost certainly derived from the word "bounce" in Riot's description (a mushroom thrown onto another mushroom bounces further). champ-data/_kits/_missing-interactions.json has propagated this into at least two teemo rows — teemo/rumble and teemo/singed both carry a "knockup-enabler: Both sides carry displacement (Noxious Trap (R) vs ...)" headline that is false on Teemo's side. Do not let any writer act on those two headlines.

Not proposed, flagged instead: full.report[].t strings duplicate breakdown text and carry the same "build MR" and male-pronoun errors for Quinn; if report[] becomes writable they should be regenerated from the corrected breakdown rather than patched.

Left alone deliberately: Quinn's W Heightened Senses carries a derived "revealsStealth" flag. Riot's text only says it reveals an area, and Teemo's passive is Invisibility rather than Camouflage — whether a plain vision reveal answers it is exactly the kind of thing the kit cannot settle, so no claim was written either way.
